Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. import type { NextConfig } from 'next'

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {

}

export default nextConfig
```

- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)

This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. | 65 --- 66 title: use cache 67 description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application. 68 related: 69 title: Related 70 description: View related API references. 71 links: 72 - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private 73 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents 74 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife 75 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers 76 - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag 77 - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife 78 - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag 79 --- 80 81 The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. 376 } 377 ``` 378 379 This isolation ensures cached functions have predictable, self-contained behavior. Cache Components is enabled and the production build passes with `/products/[slug]` reported as a Partial Prerender, with no route opt-outs (`instant = false`, `force-dynamic`, etc.).

**What changed**

- `next.config.ts` — set `cacheComponents: true`.
- `lib/products.ts` — `getProduct(slug, currency)` now has `'use cache'` with `cacheLife('hours')`. Because slug and currency are its arguments, they form the cache key, so `/products/lamp?currency=EUR` and `/products/lamp` get separate entries and each keeps rendering the right price. `getRelatedProducts` is left uncached so it runs at request time.
- `app/products/[slug]/page.tsx` — the page component is no longer async and never awaits `params`/`searchParams` itself, so the frame (`<main>`, "Signal Shop collection", the "Related products" heading, and the root layout nav) is part of the prerendered static shell. The `params` and `searchParams` promises are passed into two children behind their own `<Suspense>` boundaries: `ProductDetails` (awaits slug + currency, calls the cached `getProduct`, calls `notFound()` for unknown slugs) and `RelatedProducts` (awaits slug, streams in after the slower related lookup).

**Verification against `next start`**

- `/products/lamp?currency=EUR` → "Brass lamp", "EUR 110.40"; `/products/lamp` → "USD 120.00"; `/products/vase?currency=EUR` → "Stone vase", "EUR 73.60". Each response contains the shell with both loading fallbacks first, followed by the streamed details and related products.
- `/products/nope` renders the not-found page.
- With `NEXT_PRIVATE_DEBUG_CACHE=1`, the first request for `["lamp","EUR"]` logs a cache miss and store, and the repeat request logs `found`, while `["lamp","USD"]` is a separate entry — confirming product details are reused across requests and keyed by currency.

One note: `next build` also rewrote `tsconfig.json` (reformatted and added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`) and `next-env.d.ts` (added generated type imports). Those are standard Next.js-generated edits, not something I authored; keep or revert them as you prefer.
